entries.requirement: Every stage that produces a useful intermediate (a repaired source that compiles, a candidate, a shared fact) persists it where the next stage reads it, in the same change; a computed-and-dropped result is a defect, checked by asserting the downstream consumer actually receives it.
entries.why: S13: the fixed point compiled 131 of 477 NO_COMPILE functions and discarded the sources, so exact-tail search never saw them; writing them back produced the first exact closures of that path (10).

origin.quote: **`PR-FORWARD-AN-INTERMEDIATE-RESULT-TO-ITS-CONSUMER-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- A stage that computes a useful intermediate (a repaired source that compiles, a candidate, a fact) must persist it where the next stage reads it, in the same change that produces it. A result that is computed, scored and dropped is lost work that every later run pays again.

entries.check: a test asserts the downstream stage reads the produced artifact

entries.requirement: Every deterministic route reports eligible, admitted, executed, candidate, compiled, improved and exact separately and names the executor of each stage; a stage with no executor is reported as projected, and its savings are never reported as observed.
entries.why: S13: a FAMILY router stage existed with no input file and no executor, so 0 functions ever ran there while it looked wired and its savings were quoted.

origin.quote: **`PR-A-ROUTE-REPORTS-ITS-LIFECYCLE-WITH-A-NAMED-EXECUTOR-001`** [FACTORY] -- Every deterministic route reports eligible, admitted, executed, candidate, compiled, improved and exact as separate counts, and names the executor of each stage. A stage with no executor is "projected"; its savings are never "saved". Instance of [[T-PRODUCERLESS-FIELD-001]] on the consumer side.

entries.check: the ownership matrix lists a producer and an executor per route stage

entries.requirement: Routers, cohort builders and maturity checks decide 'resolved' from the one canonical frontier, never from a private per-lane view.
entries.why: S12C: 14 C++-certified functions were routed back to model search because maturity read a C-lane terminal.

origin.quote: **`PR-CONSUMERS-READ-THE-CANONICAL-FRONTIER-001`** [FACTORY] -- A router, cohort builder or maturity check decides "resolved" from the canonical frontier, never from a private view coupled to one lane.

entries.requirement: Before investing in a smarter search order or scheduler, measure whether the search exhausts its move set or converges to the same best node; if it does, extend the operator vocabulary instead.
entries.why: S13 W4: causal ordering equalled the frozen baseline at equal budget; 17/20 near-misses exhausted in <= 99 evaluations.

origin.quote: **`T-REORDERING-CANNOT-ADD-A-MISSING-OPERATOR-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- When a search over a finite move set exhausts or converges to the same best node, re-ordering the moves by a smarter policy changes nothing. The bottleneck is the move vocabulary. Measure exhaustion before buying a scheduler.

entries.check: an exhaustion/convergence measurement precedes any scheduler change

entries.requirement: A symbol rename or alias that turns a compile into an exact match is only accepted with byte-identical evidence for both sides plus a refused mutant; until then the result carries the alias assumption and is not counted.
entries.why: S13: 15 family members stayed alias-conditional until the target bytes were compared 22/22 words and a 1-byte mutant was refused; comments describing the bytes were rejected as evidence.

origin.quote: **`T-A-RENAMED-SYMBOL-IS-AN-ASSUMPTION-UNTIL-ITS-BYTES-ARE-COMPARED-001`** [FACTORY] -- Renaming symbols to match the target turns a compile into "exact" only if the aliasing itself is evidenced (byte-identical bodies of both sides). Until then the verdict carries the alias assumption and is not counted. A comment that describes the bytes is not the bytes.

entries.check: certify without the alias record: must be refused

entries.requirement: A generative-family report states whether hidden members test new instances or unseen parameter values, and the gate pins which; a split whose train set covers every parameter value cannot claim extrapolation.
entries.why: S13 W5: the pre-registered first-N train split already contained every parameter value; the first report claimed extrapolation.

origin.quote: **`T-A-TRAIN-SPLIT-CAN-SPAN-EVERY-PARAMETER-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- A pre-registered "first N" train split can already cover every parameter value. Hidden members then prove transfer to new instances, not to unseen values. Say which, and pin it in the gate.

entries.requirement: Before declaring target evidence absent, resolve it from existing references (code constants, manifests, knowledge vault, hashes) and verify its identity by hash; a name search that finds nothing is missing search coverage, not missing evidence.
entries.why: S13 W8 declared the target DOL bytes absent after a name search although the reconstruction code already referenced the path and the knowledge vault named the file.

origin.quote: **`T-SEARCHING-BY-NAME-MISSES-AN-ARTIFACT-THE-CODE-ALREADY-REFERENCES-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- "Not found on this host" after a name search (`*Tennis*.dol`) is not absence. Resolve the artifact from the references that already exist (code constants, manifests, the knowledge vault) before declaring evidence missing.

entries.requirement: Gates pin receipts or an independently rebuilt count, never a frontier count that legitimately advances.
entries.why: S12C/S13: gate fixtures pinned to a frontier count went red when the frontier grew and had to be relaxed.

origin.quote: **`T-A-FIXTURE-PINNED-TO-A-COUNT-THAT-LEGITIMATELY-ADVANCES-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- A gate pinned to a frontier count goes red when the frontier legitimately grows. Pin to receipts, or rebuild the count independently.

entries.check: a test asserts the consumer's call order in the production entrypoint
entries.requirement: A reconstruction capability counts as integrated only when the real production entrypoint invokes it on automatic eligible work; the gate asserts its call position inside that entrypoint and one fresh end-to-end run from it certifies something.
entries.why: S14 W2: the hot path was placed before the model pool in llm_fix run and certified 2 fresh functions at model USD 0; S13 had 132 compilable functions that never reached exact-tail search.

origin.quote: **`PR-A-CAPABILITY-IS-INTEGRATED-ONLY-WHEN-THE-PRODUCTION-ENTRY-RUNS-IT-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- A verified capability is not integrated until the real production entrypoint invokes it on an automatic, eligible workload. A producer whose output has no consumer on the production path is a defect, not a result. Detector: assert the consumer's call order inside the production entrypoint, plus one fresh end-to-end run from that entrypoint. Extends [[PR-FORWARD-AN-INTERMEDIATE-RESULT-TO-ITS-CONSUMER-001]] from a stage to the whole entrypoint.

entries.check: a mutated same-name artifact must be refused
entries.requirement: Target and evidence artifacts are resolved by content identity (size, hash, parse) into RESOLVED, MISSING_EVIDENCE, UNCOVERED or CONFLICT; a proof that depends on an artifact without recorded identity fails closed.
entries.why: S13 declared the target DOL absent after a name search; S14 W6 built the identity resolver and rejects a mutated same-name file.

origin.quote: **`PR-RESOLVE-AN-ARTIFACT-BY-CONTENT-IDENTITY-WITH-EXPLICIT-UNKNOWN-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- Identify an artifact by content (size + hash + parse), never by name or recorded path. A resolver answers one of four verdicts: RESOLVED, MISSING_EVIDENCE, UNCOVERED, CONFLICT. "Not found" is never proof of absence, and any proof that depends on the artifact fails closed when its identity is not recorded. Generalises [[T-PATH-IDENTITY-IS-NOT-RESOURCE-IDENTITY-001]] and [[T-SEARCHING-BY-NAME-MISSES-AN-ARTIFACT-THE-CODE-ALREADY-REFERENCES-001]] into a resolver contract.

entries.requirement: An operator or family enters the production hot path only after a pre-registered train/hidden split shows exact transfer, with the frozen cohort hash, the hidden results and any not-blind caveat recorded.
entries.why: S12C/S13 families transferred 12/12 on hidden members; S14 W5 promoted at n=3 with the caveat recorded.

origin.quote: **`PR-PROMOTE-AN-OPERATOR-ONLY-ON-HIDDEN-TRANSFER-001`** [FACTORY] -- Promote a reconstruction family or operator to the production hot path only after a pre-registered train/hidden split shows exact transfer. Record the frozen cohort hash and the hidden-member results. If residuals were read before the rule was written, record that as a caveat ("not blind"). See [[T-A-TRAIN-SPLIT-CAN-SPAN-EVERY-PARAMETER-001]] for what the hidden members can prove.

entries.requirement: A closure is attributed to an operator only by a before/after receipt diff that shows the pre-operator verdict; a recounted existing certificate is never a new closure.
entries.why: S14 W3 attributed frontier 1146 -> 1151 by diffing against S13 receipts that listed the 5 functions as PCT_BELOW.

origin.quote: **`T-A-RECOUNTED-CERTIFICATE-IS-NOT-A-NEW-CLOSURE-001`** [UNIVERSAL] -- A certificate that already existed, counted again, is not a new closure. Attribute a closure to an operator only by diffing receipts before and after it, and showing the verdict before the operator ran.
